newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Low telecom exposure weighs on EDP.
newsitem.headline: Low telecom exposure weighs on EDP.

text.p: Shares in state-run EDP have come under selling pressure as the utility has taken a small stake in a bid to operate Portugal's third mobile phone licence and has a premium over Spanish firm Endesa, analysts said on Thursday.

They said the stock could inch lower in the near term as Portugal's biggest listed stock came under pressure to ease tariffs and a further 60 million shares held by small investors, employees and emigrants would enter the market in September.
In early afternoon trade on Thursday, EDP was at 3,170 escudos, down 20, having broken though support at 3,180.
The government sold off a 30 percent stake of EDP, Portugal's dominant electricity provider, last month in a heavily oversubscribed first stage privatisation.
"There are a number of factors that are not favourable for EDP, which could reduce interest in the stock, even though it is a good company," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
He was referring to the small stake of EDP in a consortium led by the Sonae group's Inparsa that will bid for a third mobile phone licence later this year, and the premium of EDP over Endesa.
Positive factors for EDP are its monopoly position in the Portuguese market, and the potential for growth of energy consumption in Portugal, which is above the European average, analysts said.

"I don't see objective reasons for now that explain why EDP should fall. I know that EDP has a premium over Endesa, but EDP has advantages, as it is in a monopoly market and is relatively protected, and has greater growth potential (in terms of energy consumption)," one analyst said.

Another said: "EDP has a premium over Endesa, and Endesa is not cheap. I think that Endesa could fall ahead of its privatisation, because it is expensive and runs the risk of running into problems in the placing."
State holding company Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales (Sepi) is to sell 25-35 percent of Endesa's capital in a mammoth public share offering in the autumn.
One analyst, who asked not to be identified, forecast EDP's Price Earnings Ratio (PER) for 1998 at 19.8, compared with 17.8 for Endesa and 13.6 for another Spanish utility, Iberdrola .

A factor weighing on EDP's share price in the near term was the addition to the market of 60 million shares, the tranche in the privatisation reserved for small investors, employees and emigrants, on September 17 this year.
But some analysts said that institutions may be hoping to snap up these shares cheaply.

Analysts said that if a consortium including EDP wins a bid for a controlling stake in Brazil's Bahia state power utility Coelba, due to be sold on Thursday, it ran the risk that its returns would be diluted as the real currency was overvalued.
Six-month results of EDP are not due to be released until mid-August, a company source said. Analysts have made no forecast due to a lack of figures from the same year-ago period.
Analysts expect that EDP will make a net profit of between 88 and 90 billion escudos for 1997, up from 81 billion for 1996.
Endesa's six-month results, announced on Wednesday, dropped by 3.9 percent year-on-year to 78.588 billion pesetas.
